section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: The OS_MMUControl SWI was updated for RISC OS 3.7 to add another reason code (reason code 1 to flush the cache). This has been extended with Kernel 9.80 to allow the write buffer to be drained. OS_MMUControl 0 has been extended to return errors if the MMU control register values are incompatible with the CPU or with the operating system.

entry.register-use:
Operation and flags:
Operation Flags (others dependent on operation)

use.p: This SWI is used to perform MMU operations. Consult the operation codes for more details.

entry.register-use:
0 (set MMU control register) + flags:
Operation (0) Reserved (must be zero) Do not mirror D Cache bit into I Cache bit

use.p: This SWI is used to change the state of the MMU control register in a processor independent manner. Any flags which are not changeable on the processor will return an error message. Any flags which are not changeable because the operating system does not support that configuration will return an error message.

For compatibility with earlier systems, unless bit 31 of the flags in R0 is set, the D cache bit will be mirrored into the I cache bit. If bit 31 of the flags in R0 is set, the D cache bit will only control that one bit. For processors which do not provide an I cache, this has no effect.

entry.register-use:
1 (cache and TLB operations) + flags:
Operation (1) Reserved (must be zero) Drain write buffer Flush a single entry (otherwise a complete flush) Flush processor TLBs Flush processor cache (both I and D cache)
Logical address, if R0 bit 29 set

use.p: This call implements platform independent cache and/or TLB flushing.
Currently, bit 29 is ignored, so that only whole flushing of caches and/or TLBs are supported. A cache will be cleaned before flushing, where the processor supports a write-back cache.

This reason code is not re-entrant. Interrupts are not disabled during the flush, so the cache or TLB flush can only be considered to be complete with respect to logical addresses that are not currently involved in interrupts.
The 'drain write buffer' flag was introduced in Kernel 9.80.
